question: Does positive nearest-neighbor support coupling reduce rigid-translation normal-field error by at least 1.5 times relative to the best uncoupled directional support in the declared analytic non-planar coil surrogate, at equal stiffness trace and within the declared load-conflict, compliance, linearization, and resolution limits?
assumptions: The eight identical non-planar filamentary coils and toroidal sampling surface are an analytic mechanism probe, not an optimized stellarator equilibrium or a representation of a named device.
Each coil has only three rigid local translation degrees of freedom; bending, casing and conductor strain, preload, joints, buckling, fatigue, and the surrounding support structure are excluded.
The complete orthogonal unit-load basis is a direction-neutral probe, not a probability distribution or reactor load spectrum; the calculated symmetric mutual-coil force is checked separately.
The trace of the dimensionless stiffness matrix is a deliberately weak equal-resource proxy and does not establish equal mass, stress, cost, access, or manufacturability.

Every requirement is a nominal research gate over the exact checker output. Passing would justify only a second gate on published geometry; it would not establish a practical support, physical validation, novelty, patentability, safety, or operational fitness.

requirements.statement: Exact displaced-geometry RMS normal-field-error reduction is at least 1.5 times the best uncoupled directional support.
Exact normal-field error under the calculated nominal mutual-coil load is no more than 1.25 times the uncoupled control.
Worst compliance is no more than twice the unit isotropic support.
Worst retained linear-sensitivity error relative to exact displaced-geometry Biot-Savart recalculation is no more than 10 percent.
The coupled-versus-uncoupled reduction changes by no more than 15 percent between the declared coarse and fine discretizations.
The magnetic sensitivity matrix changes by no more than 2 percent when the central-difference step is halved.
At least 10 percent of the selected stiffness trace is expressed through nearest-neighbor coupling.
